title: U.S. House · Georgia's 5th Congressional District
area: Most of the city of Atlanta and surrounding Fulton County.

context.text: Incumbent Nikema Williams (D), first elected in 2020, won the Democratic primary over Arnetress Beatty with 88% of the vote. John Salvesen advanced from the Republican primary unopposed.

candidates.name: Nikema Williams
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary over Arnetress Beatty, 88.0% to 12.0%.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Georgia's 5th Congressional District (since 2021)

summary.text: Nikema Williams is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Georgia's 5th Congressional District, first elected in 2020 to succeed the late Rep. John Lewis. Before Congress she worked in public policy and advocacy for Planned Parenthood Southeast and the National Domestic Workers Alliance, served in the Georgia State Senate, and chaired the Democratic Party of Georgia. She is seeking re-election to a fourth term.

background.text: Born in Columbus, Georgia, in 1978 and raised in Smiths Station, Alabama; she lives in Atlanta.
Graduated from Talladega College with a degree in biology, according to her official biography.
Moved to Atlanta in 2002 and joined the Young Democrats of Georgia; served as first vice chair of the Democratic Party of Georgia from 2011.

Worked as vice president of Public Policy for Planned Parenthood Southeast, deputy director of civic engagement for the National Domestic Workers Alliance, and deputy executive director of Care in Action before being elected to Congress.
Won a 2017 special election to the Georgia State Senate and represented District 39 from 2017 to 2021.
Was elected chair of the Democratic Party of Georgia in January 2019, was re-elected in 2023, and stepped down in 2025.
After Rep. John Lewis died in July 2020, the Democratic Party of Georgia selected her to replace him on the November ballot; she won the November 3, 2020 general election with 85.1% of the vote.

Serves on the House Financial Services Committee and, per her official biography, is Whip of the Democratic Women's Caucus and a member of the Congressional Black Caucus, Progressive Caucus, and New Democrat Coalition.
Won re-election in 2022 and 2024 (85.7% over John Salvesen in 2024) and the 2026 Democratic primary with 88.0% over Arnetress Beatty.
According to her official biography, she is married to Leslie Small and has a son.

priorities.text: Says she is committed to amplifying the voice of the people, breaking down barriers to voting, and ensuring the integrity of elections.
Says she is committed to the promise of universal, quality health care coverage and will continue fighting to ensure people can access medical services from prenatal to mental health care.
Says she advocates for student debt cancellation for federal borrowers and for policies to bring immediate relief to especially debt-burdened borrowers.

positions.summary: Her official site says she co-sponsored Medicare for All legislation and is committed to universal, quality health care coverage.
positions.quote: In Congress, I co-sponsored Medicare for All legislation and I am committed to the promise of universal, quality health care coverage.

positions.summary: Her official site says guns should be kept away from people who pose a threat to themselves or others, in support of federal red-flag legislation.
positions.quote: We can help prevent other people from living through that horror by keeping guns away from people who pose a threat to themselves or others.

positions.summary: Introduced a congressional resolution affirming reproductive freedom, including abortion access, as a human right and said state abortion bans endanger lives.
positions.quote: That is why this resolution is important: it affirms that reproductive freedom is a fundamental human right according to the United States' own law and that state abortion bans are violating federal law and endangering the lives of women.

positions.summary: Said she supports restoring fairness in the tax system by raising rates on the wealthiest individuals and the biggest corporations.
positions.quote: Congresswoman Williams also supports restoring fairness in the tax system – raising rates on the wealthiest individuals and the biggest corporations, many of whom currently pay little to no federal income tax – to help pay for this legislation.

positions.summary: Said she supports investments including child care and free universal pre-K as part of the Build Back Better agenda.
positions.quote: Congresswoman Williams supports inclusion of investments that enjoy broad, bipartisan levels of support among the American people, including investments in child care, home health care, paid family and medical leave, free universal pre-K, the Biden Child Tax Credit, workforce development, expanding Medicare benefits, closing the Medicaid coverage gap, addressing the climate crisis, services for veterans, and more.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Financial Services in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Introduced a congressional resolution affirming reproductive freedom, including abortion access, as a human right, co-led with Reps. Alma Adams, Troy Carter, Greg Casar and Jennifer McClellan.
Reintroduced the Storing All Firearms Effectively and Safely (SAFES) Act, creating a refundable tax credit for purchasing a gun safe to safely store firearms.

candidates.name: John Salvesen
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary unopposed.

summary.text: John Salvesen, who goes by Bongo, is the Republican nominee for Georgia's 5th Congressional District and was also the party's nominee in 2024, when he lost to Nikema Williams. Ballotpedia lists his career experience in the construction industry. Little other biographical information is publicly available.

background.text: Ballotpedia lists his birthplace as Burbank, California; in his 2024 Candidate Connection survey he described himself as originally from South Jersey and said he has lived in Atlanta since 1994.
Ballotpedia lists a graduate degree from Santa Monica College in 1989 and career experience in the construction industry.
Was the Republican nominee in 2024, advancing from the May 21, 2024 primary unopposed and losing the general election to Williams, 14.3% to 85.7%.
Advanced from the May 19, 2026 Republican primary for the 5th District.

priorities.text: Says Georgia's election system is susceptible to being hacked and should be replaced by paper ballots.
Says he is strongly against attempts at 15-minute cities and the elimination of cash.
Says there are food ingredients the FDA should not have approved.

candidates.researchNotes: Priorities from his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. His survey answers do not directly address the tracked issues. The campaign website named in the survey (bongoforcongress.com) now serves unrelated content and was not cited.
